title: final-japanese-reassessment-replacement-20260731
rawUserRequest: Japanese is mandatory for the repository's intended adopters. Before release, conduct a comprehensive final Japanese capability reassessment; correct any problem through its own complete Work Item lifecycle, keep all claims evidence-based, and continue the authorized serial plan without pausing for non-required confirmation.

declaredIntent.summary: Produce a fresh exact-source final Japanese repository-governance capability assessment before release, without overclaiming or advancing publication.

outOfScope: Publishing a release, creating or moving a tag, or changing provider release state.
Claiming general Japanese model fluency, native-human translation review, provider behavior, enterprise compliance, or external reviewer identity.
Rewriting archived Work Item evidence or deleting branches/worktrees outside this Work Item lifecycle.

sources.reason: WI-16 is a mandatory pre-release Japanese capability gate; any gap must be corrected and reassessed before publication.
The remediation baseline requires an independent Japanese assessment and leaves release blocked until it closes.
The recorded remaining sequence places final Japanese reassessment before release and plan cleanup.
Deterministic assessment, source binding, blocking findings, and explicit non-claims.
Regression evidence for Japanese corpus, source binding, release-gate wiring, and report drift.
Human-readable Japanese capability matrix and limitations.
Generated pre-release documentation alignment evidence that must be refreshed when the Japanese release-gate report changes.
Human-readable projection of the generated pre-release documentation alignment evidence.

riskAssessment.reason: Japanese capability is mandatory for intended adopters. A stale, English-inferred, or overclaimed assessment could incorrectly permit publication.

executionDecision.reason: The user has authorized the plan. The assessment must fail closed on blocking evidence and must not release.

preReviewWarnings: Review source-binding freshness, Japanese-only evidence, high-risk STOP boundaries, and non-claims; do not infer general Japanese fluency.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A fresh assessment is source-bound to this Work Item's current repository evidence and identifies this final reassessment rather than a historic Work Item.

Japanese corpus, high-risk STOP boundaries, Wizard/CLI, Status, Task Outcome, installed adopter lifecycle, documentation, uninstall runtime, three-language structure, and release-gate paths have deterministic executable evidence; any failed case remains blocking.

The machine-readable and Markdown assessment documents agree, include the exact source evidence digest, and preserve explicit limits on general fluency, human translation quality, provider behavior, and external controls.

Source-binding, report-drift, expected-source mismatch, Japanese capability regressions, and dependent pre-release documentation-alignment regeneration pass; required governance checks and fresh Hosted CI pass before this Work Item is closed.
An active Chinese task report is sent before archive, then this Work Item completes a dedicated PR, merge, Closure Receipt, and local/remote work-branch cleanup.
guidelines: Use repository evidence and executable tests; do not infer Japanese capability from English results.
Treat missing, stale, or non-executable Japanese evidence as blocking until a corrective Work Item closes and this assessment is rerun.
Preserve explicit non-claims: no general model fluency, human translation quality, provider behavior, sandboxing, enterprise compliance, or external identity claims.
Keep the machine-readable and Markdown reports derived from the same assessment facts and bind evidence to repository-relative file bytes.

intent.problem: The current Japanese assessment identifies a historic Work Item and may be stale after subsequent source changes. Japanese is mandatory for the repository's intended adopters, so a release cannot rely on a prior result without an exact current evidence binding.
constraints: Assess only deterministic repository-governance Japanese capabilities and explicitly retain limitations.
Do not publish, tag, mutate provider release state, or bypass a blocking finding.
If an evidence gap is found, create and close a separate corrective Work Item before declaring this final assessment current.
intent.rationale: A fresh source-bound assessment makes the Japanese release gate auditable and prevents an older report or English-only inference from being treated as current capability proof.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The final report is regenerated from the exact current source and identifies this Work Item rather than a historic assessment.
scenarioCoverage.expected: JSON and Markdown reports have matching facts, current source-file digests, this Work Item identity, and no stale-report drift.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Regenerate both reports; run Japanese report-drift and exact expected-source regressions against the committed Work Item Head.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Japanese and mixed-language corpus inputs include high-risk, Unknown, encoded, Unicode, hidden-instruction, and absurd requests.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Authority boundaries and STOP/human-confirmation outcomes remain evidence-backed and fail closed for every high-risk corpus entry.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the Japanese capability, input-trust, corpus, and real absurd/injection test suites.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Japanese engineers use supported Wizard/CLI, Status, Outcome, installation, calibration, recovery, uninstall, and document paths.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Each supported surface has direct executable Japanese evidence; missing or English-inferred evidence stays blocking.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run Japanese Wizard, Status, Outcome, adopter-lifecycle, documentation, and Trust Layer regression suites.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A claim asks for general Japanese fluency, human translation quality, provider behavior, or external controls beyond repository evidence.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The assessment retains its limitation and does not promote it to a repository capability or release authorization.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Inspect both regenerated reports and run non-claim/report-drift regression tests.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The regenerated matrix has one or more blocking findings.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Release stays blocked and the finding is routed to a dedicated corrective Work Item; the assessment is not marked passed.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Inspect blockingFindings directly; only a machine-proved empty list may complete this reassessment.
